title: Quantum Teleportation Over a Noisy Relay Channel
abstract: Quantum teleportation and Bell measurements are considered in a noisy relay setting. We introduce two quantum relay-channel models with closed-form capacity formulas, motivated by the canonical quantum communication protocols of teleportation and superdense coding. In both models, the sender transmits a qubit, while the relay observes side information about the Pauli errors that occur in the channel and communicates with the receiver through an orthogonal rate-limited link. We develop a compress-forward coding scheme in which the relay compresses the Pauli-error sequence into bins and sends the bin index to the receiver. The receiver uses this partial error information to reduce the effective channel noise before quantum decoding. We show that this strategy is optimal by establishing matching converse bounds for both models.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes quantum communication over noisy relay channels, modeling scenarios like quantum teleportation and superdense coding. It derives optimal capacity formulas for specific noise types (dephasing, depolarizing) by proposing a novel compress-forward coding scheme. The work establishes the fundamental limits on how much quantum information can be reliably transmitted when the channel quality is degraded by noise and limited by a classical relay link.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the achievable quantum and classical communication capacities for quantum teleportation and superdense coding when transmitted over a noisy quantum relay channel.
main_result: The authors derive closed-form capacity formulas for both dephasing and depolarizing relay channels, showing that the optimal strategy involves a compress-forward coding scheme.
method: The capacity is determined by establishing matching converse bounds and constructing explicit achievable coding schemes using techniques from quantum information theory.
model_or_system: The study models quantum communication over two specific noisy relay channels: a dephasing channel (for teleportation) and a depolarizing channel (for superdense coding). The relay observes side information about the Pauli errors.
key_observables: Quantum Capacity ($C_Q$), Entanglement-Assisted Capacity ($C_{EA}$), and the rate limit of the classical link ($R_0$).
important_parameters: Error probabilities (e.g., $q_Z$, $q_X$, $q$), and the classical rate $R_0$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the classical link capacity $R_0$ is the limiting factor, and the achievability proofs rely on the existence of codes achieving vanishing error.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the quantum capacity vs. dephasing probability for the dephasing channel, and the entanglement-assisted capacity vs. depolarization probability for the depolarizing channel.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the two quantum relay-channel models, develops the compress-forward coding scheme, derives the closed-form capacity formulas, and proves optimality using converse bounds.
why_interesting: While focused on abstract quantum channels, the principles of noise mitigation and capacity scaling derived here are fundamental to understanding error correction and communication in complex quantum systems, which has parallels in open quantum systems.
